name: GPXHooks rebalances protocol liquidity at the manipulated spot price
summary: GoldPesa's Uniswap v4 hook GPXHooks re-centres its protocol-owned GPX/USDC position from beforeSwap whenever an hour has passed since the last rebalance, burning the position and re-minting all its USDC from the pool's current spot price. With a Morpho USDC flash loan the attacker bought GPX to raise the price, swapped again to trigger the rebalance at that price, and sold the GPX back into the re-placed liquidity, taking 114,428 USDC.
notes: The hook's own rebalance writes (position id, lower tick, reserves, last rebalance) are automated live values, not resets; mintInitialLiquidity and setAddresses ran in the deployment block. The 126 earlier rebalances were triggered by ordinary swaps: none moved USDC out of the pool beyond a plain GPX sale. The attacker's repeat 0xa7910f17 reverted.
Loss is the pool's USDC outflow net of the swap fees the hook paid to GoldPesa's own pawn and owner addresses; the position's GPX went back to the hook.
